transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park. I'm Dr. Miller, the resident on the surgical team. I wanted to come by and check on you and talk about why you're back with us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, hi. Yeah. I just... the nurse told me something happened with my discharge?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, there was a bit of a situation with the timing of when you left the hospital yesterday. Things didn't go quite right with the scheduling.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't really know. I just felt the wound starting to leak and then it got really red, so I came back to the ER. Was I not supposed to leave yet?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I can tell you're feeling a bit overwhelmed right now. It's a lot to deal with, especially being here on your own.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I didn't know if I did something wrong. Like, maybe I didn't take care of it right at home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you did everything we told you to do. It's just that the process was a bit rushed on our end. I am sorry for any confusion that caused. We were incredibly busy yesterday and things just got mixed up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Okay. So, did I leave too early?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with the protocol timing. We had some confusion regarding the window for discharge.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm kind of confused. Did the doctors make a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was more of a system overlap. The paperwork and the timing didn't align perfectly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why is my wound doing this then? Is it because of the timing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's possible that the timing contributed to how the wound is looking now. We're going to get it cleaned up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I'm a bit scared. I don't really know who to call. My parents are in another state and I don't know if I should be worried about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're anxious about this. It's scary when things don't go as planned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah. I just want to know what happened. Was I supposed to stay another six hours? The nurse mentioned something about six hours.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some irregularities in the discharge timeline. It wasn't the ideal window.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So it was a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry that it felt confusing. Like I said, the ward was slammed yesterday and the coordination just wasn't there.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess. I just don't want it to get infected.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We're on top of it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I have to stay overnight again? Or can I go home once this is cleaned?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure yet. We'll have to see how the wound looks after the cleaning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned. Someone will probably let you know later on or maybe we'll send an update to your portal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't really check the portal that much. Can you tell me now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to get to my other patients right now, so I can't give you a definitive answer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what about the mistake? Do I need to tell my insurance or... I don't even know how this works.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Don't worry about that. We'll handle the administrative side of things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like I'm not really sure what's going on.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a bit of a muddle, but we're fixing it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have the team check on you soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's just wrap this up for now. I'll check back in later.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I really have to get to my other patients', 'Let's just wrap this up for now').

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'system overlap'.

A.justification: Responsibility is deflected to the system and the busy ward ('the ward was slammed', 'system overlap', 'coordination just wasn't there').

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions twice ('overwhelmed', 'anxious') and engages with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders ('stay tuned', 'we'll have to see') and refuses to give a definitive answer.
